wu: Warm-up: 'Find Someone Who...' game. Students walk around asking peers 'Did you [eat couscous yesterday]?' and mark names on their bingo sheet. Teacher models first question with flashcard of couscous.
wuAlt: Alternative 1: 'Past Tense Ball Toss'. Teacher says a verb (e.g., 'go'), students toss a ball and say past form ('went') in pairs.
Alternative 2: 'Memory Chain'. Teacher starts 'Yesterday I ate...', each student adds one food item in past tense.
pres: Presentation: Show New Year's Eve flashcards (fireworks, family, food). Model sentences: 'Last year, I was at home with my family. We were happy.' Elicit time expressions (yesterday, last year). Check understanding with thumbs-up/down for true/false sentences about the teacher.
presAlt: Alternative 1: Use a short video clip of New Year celebrations. Pause and ask 'Where were they? What were they doing?'
Alternative 2: Draw a timeline on the board with 'now' and 'last year'. Students write sentences about themselves using 'was/were'.
prac: Guided practice: 'Past Tense Tic-Tac-Toe'. In pairs, students choose a square with a subject (e.g., 'I') and make a 'was/were' sentence. Correct sentences get an X/O. Teacher monitors for errors and provides sentence frames.
pracAlt: Alternative 1: 'Verb Be Bingo'. Students fill grids with 'was/were' sentences. Teacher calls out prompts (e.g., 'at school yesterday') for students to mark.
Alternative 2: 'Find the Mistake'. Teacher writes 5 sentences with 'was/were' errors. Students correct them in pairs.
ls: Listening slot: Play a 1-minute audio of a teen describing last New Year's Eve. Students listen and circle correct 'was/were' sentences on their worksheet. Then, listen again and write one detail they heard about the person's celebration.
re: Reactivation game: 'Past Taction'. Teacher calls out a past verb (e.g., 'ate'), students mime the action and say the past form. Speed increases to keep energy high after the break.
prod: Production task: 'New Year's Quiz Swap'. Students write 5 quiz questions about the past (e.g., 'Were you born in Oujda?'). Swap with a partner and answer. Then, share one interesting fact about their partner with the class.
rw: Reading and writing slot: Read a short story (40 words) about a child's New Year's Eve. Underline all 'was/were' and past verbs. Then, write 6 sentences about their own last weekend using 'was/were' and time markers.
st: Story/Song + Goodbye: Play 'Auld Lang Syne' instrumental while showing New Year images. Close with: 'Today we learned to talk about the past with was/were. Thank you, class!'
g: Students mime past actions (e.g., 'ate') for others to guess the verb.
Teams race to write correct 'was/were' sentences on the board.
Students sit in a circle and take turns adding to a story using past tense.
Teacher says a past verb, students find a partner and say the past form together.
Teams race to write 5 sentences using 'was/were' about a given topic.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a 10-sentence story about their best New's Eve.
Support: Use sentence frames like 'I was ___.' 'We were ___.' with word banks.
hw: Option 1: Record a 1-minute voice note about your childhood using 'was/were'.
Option 2: Write 5 resolutions with 'will' (e.g., 'I will learn English') and 5 with 'going to' (e.g., 'I am going to study more').
Option 3: Draw a picture of last weekend and write 5 sentences about it using past tense.
tip: Use Moroccan cultural references (e.g., 'Aid al-Adha', 'Green March') to make past tense practice relatable and boost engagement.
